card.title: Conduction to Stefan-Boltzmann — three highways of heat

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Heat travels three ways: conduction (molecule-to-molecule in solids, metered by thermal conductivity K), convection (bulk fluid motion — hot rises), radiation (electromagnetic waves, no medium needed). An ideal black body absorbs and emits perfectly; its total radiated power follows Stefan-Boltzmann, E = σT⁴.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: conduction: Q/t = K·A·(ΔT)/L (K in W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹)  ·  rate of flow: joule/second = watt  ·  Stefan–Boltzmann: E = σT⁴, σ = 5.67×10⁻⁸ W·m⁻²·K⁻⁴ (T in kelvin, total power P = σAeT⁴)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The conduction formula needs steady state (linear temperature gradient, no heat storage in the rod). K measurement (Searle's method) assumes one-dimensional flow with insulated sides. Stefan's law needs absolute temperature and a black (or grey, with emissivity e) surface radiating into cold surroundings.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Metals conduct (free electrons), gases insulate (wool, fur trap air, not heat). Heater supplying 4200 J in 4 s: rate = 1050 J/s = 1050 W (NEB 2023). Doubling absolute temperature multiplies radiated power 16× — the T⁴ leverage behind stars and furnaces.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: 4200 J in 4 s → rate of heat flow = Q/t = 4200/4 = 1050 joule per second; SI unit watt (W) (NEB 2023, 3 marks). Conduction variant: same rate through a rod reads K = (Q/t)·L/(A·ΔT) — one formula, both directions.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Conduction's linear law breaks with large ΔT or non-steady heating. Convection resists formulas (geometry-dependent, empirical). Real bodies are grey (e < 1, wavelength-dependent); Stefan's T⁴ also demands net exchange — a body at room temperature in a room-temperature enclosure radiates and receives equally.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: K from Searle's bar: steady heat Q/t through cross-section A over length L with end-temperatures T₁, T₂ gives K = (Q/t)·L/[A(T₁−T₂)] — measure the flow by the water calorimeter at the cold end. Stefan's law is empirical (Boltzmann derived it thermodynamically); Planck's quantum law explains it.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'Rate of heat flow' = Q/t in watts, always. Conduction questions: write K·A·ΔT/L and solve the fraction. T⁴ questions: convert to kelvin FIRST — the commonest lost mark. Black body = perfect absorber AND perfect emitter.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): 4200 J in 4 s — rate + SI unit. NEB 2022 (2): define rate of heat flow + formula + unit. Conduction/K-measurement and black-body/Stefan statements complete the set.
